vectors.title: an approval repeated by the same approver after the commit does not run a second effect and is answered like the first
spec: specs/task-consent/decision/0.2/spec.md (consumer 10: record the approval idempotently per approver)
vectors.clarify: The specification asks for idempotent recording but also says a request that was already decided is noPending; which answer a repeat after the commit gets is not stated. The vector asserts the repeated answer and no second effect. Not gating.

vectors.title: a request from an enrolled executor is answered with a response of the request type carrying status prompted, and one prompt is raised
spec: specs/task-consent/request/0.1/spec.md (consumer 7: return a response with status prompted or refused)
vectors.clarify: Vector over-reads: the text is clear (consumer 6, spec.md:154: refuse with notEligible when the device is not a member of approverSet; consumer 7, spec.md:155: #response with status prompted or refused), but membership of the named approverSet is set by the policy (spec.md:197), which the harness does not declare; the vector asserts prompted, which presumes membership. The suite can fix this by declaring membership (governance declaration, docs/04 section 19, consent.approverSet) and gating on it, or by asserting only a #response with status prompted or refused. Not gating.

vectors.title: a decision that leaves the quorum short is answered with a response of the decision type (status pending) or with a hold (trust-task-next-step), and a repeat by the same approver is not another approver's approval: the quorum is completed only by the other approver's decision
spec: specs/task-consent/decision/0.2/spec.md (consumer 10: record the approval idempotently per approver, and at the threshold of distinct approvers...; Response status pending; framework 8.6, a held task is answered with trust-task-next-step)
vectors.clarify: A decision that leaves the threshold unmet is answered with the specification's `pending` status or, equally, with a trust-task-next-step hold (the framework's own vocabulary for a held task; the hold rule of 8.6 is checked); the two differ in form only. Which one an implementation uses is not asserted. Not gating.
